events.text:
## Recommendation

- Go to **Grand Haven** by boat. Fish 100-200 ft of water, with lines about 85-140 ft down.
- Run white or green fly combinations and green spoons, which the latest reports say worked.
- **Muskegon** is the close second. Fish 130-210 ft of water with rotators in white or green fly combinations.
- Skip South Haven and St. Joseph unless you're already there. Boat fishing was only fair at both.

## Why

- Grand Haven boats had the best recent report: the Sept 21 report rated them good, with fish 85-140 ft down in 100-200 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2026-09-21).
- Muskegon boats were also rated good on Sept 21, at 85-130 ft down in 130-210 ft of water (Muskegon, 2022-09-21).
- I'd expect the cold water pushed in by the north and east winds to hold the fish in those depths, but this is my inference, not something a report says.

## Evidence

**Ratings for boat salmon this week (0-4):**
- Grand Haven: **3** (good). The Sept 21 report rated boats good (Grand Haven, 2022-09-21).
- Muskegon: **3** (good). The Sept 21 report rated Chinook boats good (Muskegon, 2022-09-21). The same report said boats trolling near the breakwalls were slow.
- South Haven: **2** (average). Best water was "beyond 120 feet," with spoons producing most fish (South Haven, 2022-09-21).
- St. Joseph: **2** (average). "Salmon anglers had fair fishing… most productive water was around 120 feet" (St. Joseph, 2022-09-21). That is a thin report.

**Recent reports:**
- Grand Haven, Sept 21: boats in 100-200 ft, fish 85-140 ft down, "White paddles with green or white flies worked very well along with green spoons." The pier was slow (Grand Haven, 2022-09-21).
- Muskegon, Sept 21: boats in 130-210 ft, fish 85-130 ft down, "Rotators with white or green fly combinations worked well" (Muskegon, 2022-09-21).

**Past seasons:**
- The similar-weeks search matched only one report: St. Joseph, Sept 21, rated average. It is not enough to show a typical pattern, so I'm not leaning on history.

**Conditions now:**
- The live feed was unavailable, so the conditions below are a summary of the week before today.
- Buoy surface water at Grand Haven and Muskegon was about 62 F, down 21 F over the week. Satellite water near the piers was about 68 F, down 7 F (Grand Haven and Muskegon, week before 2022-09-27).
- Upwelling-favorable wind (north to east, 8+ mph) blew 62 hours in Grand Haven's week and 37 hours in the last three days. The week's gusts reached 36 mph (Grand Haven, week before 2022-09-27).
- General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant): a sharp drop in buoy temperature signals upwelling, which can bring salmon toward piers and river mouths. Chinook in early fall often hold in water of 55 F or less.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from Sept 21, six days old. Conditions can change quickly this time of year.
- The 21 F buoy drop at Grand Haven and Muskegon looks large next to the satellite's 7 F. Treat the buoy number with caution.
- I don't have a forecast for this weekend. Check the wind before you go: gusts reached 36 mph this past week, which is rough for a small boat.
- The South Haven and St. Joseph ratings rest on one or two report lines each.

## Sources

- Grand Haven and Muskegon, Sept 21 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32e369d
- South Haven and St. Joseph, Sept 21 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32e369d
- Sept 14 bulletin (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90
